analyst_view.overall: Early view: Como have a strong home record (one goal conceded in four home league games) and play this five days after hosting AEK Athens in the Champions League. Juventus play only three days after hosting Omonia in the Europa League and have a long injury list, including Yildiz, Cambiaso and Locatelli; Kalulu's thigh injury was put at about three weeks by one report, so he may be close. Como changed their usual style to sit deep at Inter, and it did not work.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean slightly lower: Como's home games have averaged only about 1.4 goals, and Juventus's games are among the lowest-scoring in the league at about 2.5. A tired Juventus three days after Omonia is unlikely to open the game up.

corners.text: The site expects 9.4 corners. I lean higher: Como's home games have averaged about 10.6 corners, and Juventus's away games about 13, with Juventus winning over nine a game themselves. Both sides play a lot of possession in wide areas.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. Como are one of the least-booked teams in the league, but Juventus's games have produced a few bookings for dissent lately, including Spalletti and Kolo Muani at Fiorentina. Those cancel out, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site expects 25.9 shots. I lean higher: Como's home games have averaged about 29 shots and Juventus's away games about 30. Both sides want the ball, and Como take about 19 shots a game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Como's home games have averaged about seven on target and Juventus's away games about 9.5, so the number sits between them. I see nothing pointing either way.
